title: hotfix: improve SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover under load
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: tune SLO enforcer backoff, add per-region soft-thresholds and jitter to load-shedding logic to prevent cascading failovers under bursty load. Improves availability during regional hotspots.
description: Context: In high-concurrency bursts we observed the SLO enforcer entering a pathological backoff state: aggressive global backoff + immediate regional failover led to cascading capacity pressure in target regions and prolonged load-shedding windows. This caused customer-facing errors during a 2026-02-17 incident. This patchset introduces three changes: 1) move from aggressive exponential backoff to a capped, jittered backoff with per-region token buckets to limit simultaneous failovers; 2) introduce a soft-threshold mode for load-shedding that prefers connection-level queueing and graded shedding instead of immediate hard rejects; 3) add additional metrics and tracing hooks to better observe per-region failover rate and backoff state transitions. The PR includes unit and integration tests, an observability dashboard update, and a short canary rollout config. All changes are backward-compatible and guarded behind a feature flag defaulting on in main. Summary of changes in this PR: - Implement capped jittered backoff algorithm in SLO enforcer. - Add per-region token bucket controller for failover permits. - Replace immediate hard-shed path with graded_soft_shed mode and associated config. - Add metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_state, slo_enforcer.region_permit_acquire, slo_enforcer.soft_shed_rate. - Update canary rollout (2% -> 25%) and add smoke tests. Motivation: reduce cascading regional failovers and shorten recovery time during bursty traffic while preserving SLO enforcement guarantees. Rollout plan: apply to dedicated + hosted canary at 2% for 1 hour, monitor new metrics, then escalate to 25% for 24 hours before full rollout. If any regression in latency or error rate, rollback via feature flag.
